fact: Capacity reports Telecom Egypt completed SEA-ME-WE-6 landings at Port Said and Ras Ghareb in July 2025.
Capacity reports an activated 2Africa link connecting Egypt to France via Italy, with Cisco, in January 2025 (Telecom Egypt).
Agence Ecofin, citing Submarine Cable Map, says about twenty cables are connected to Egypt, with five more systems under construction.

Ahram Online says Egypt hosts around 15 active international submarine cable systems, the most in Africa, with 2Africa linking Mediterranean and Red Sea routes through Egypt (published Dec 2025 proxy, byline 9 Feb 2026).
Al-Ahram Gate reports Telecom Egypt, with Cisco, activated capacity on the 2Africa Mediterranean link from Port Said, Egypt to Marseille, France via Genoa, Italy.

Telecom Egypt says the 2Africa cable lands in Egypt at Ras Ghareb on the Red Sea and Port Said on the Mediterranean, joined by two trans-Egypt terrestrial routes, and its core infrastructure is complete; as_of is the press release date.

Telecom Egypt says the Coral Bridge subsea cable, a 15 km link from its Taba landing point in Sinai to Aqaba Digital Hub in Jordan, has been launched and activated; no launch date given, so as_of is the release date.
Telecom Egypt states that 14 subsea cable systems land in Egypt's 10 cable stations, linked by 10 terrestrial routes (stations not named).
Telecom Egypt's WeConnect platform lets partners click-to-order cross-connectivity between the 14 subsea cable systems at its 10 Egyptian cable stations on an open and neutral model.

DataCenterDynamics reports that the original Seacom cable, launched in 2009 with Tata Communications, runs from Egypt through the Red Sea to Djibouti, then branches west to the Indian Ocean and south to South Africa; no Egyptian landing station is named.
